title: Hall without a name on the plan
subtitle: two-storey hall at the back of the maze · Xiyang Lou

model.line: Modelled from plate 5 of 1783-86 and the plan S01: the walls follow S01's lines, set into the block whose size the archive figures give (58.56 × 88.64 m, S310) at the place of today's rebuilt maze; heights and forms read on plate 5 (C). No picture of the maze before 1987 shows it from the ground; the Yangshi Lei plan 样337-146 is not in hand.
rows: 171 runs of carved grey brick, 1233 m, 1.2 × 0.6 m (S310, B): the pattern traced on the plan S01 (plan_readings.csv) and set into the block of 58.56 × 88.64 m (S310, today's rebuild; Q292); a framed band of raised keys for the 卐字 carving, clipped trees of three tiers on the copings (plate 5, C)
276 m, 1.5 m high (C), open at the south gate (花园门 XY03, the kit's), at a west and an east gate with pineapple-finial piers and iron leaves, and at the north behind the hall (S01; plate 5, C)

a round drum 12 m across, its top 3.8 m up, with carved panels; a straight flight to a landing, then two curved flights of 20 steps climbing round the drum behind a carved parapet with a balustrade to meet at its back (plate 5; S01's ring 17.2 m and flight, C)

an octagon 6.4 m across, four arched large faces and four small ones with windows (S258, B), corner columns 5.2 m, a tiled skirt, a ribbed dome, an open lantern and a gilt ball 16.7 m above the ground (plate 5, C); a vase inside (assumed)
14.9 × 10.1 m (S01 on the block), two storeys (S02, B) to 7 m, a hipped Chinese roof with finials (plate 5, C), its terrace and flight; the walls carried from the group (assumed)
four weeping pagoda trees in round curbs at the inner corners (S310, B; places from S01, C); a half-round basin before the hall (S01, C)
the paving of the paths, the hall's façades, the pavilion's back faces and the vase inside it, the basin: carried round or guessed (C, the pale tint with conf=1)

searched: This block has no name on the plan or in the texts, so no source can be searched for it by name.
